fieldsRead.text: Biomedical Engineering at TU/e combines biology, chemistry, physics, mathematics and computing to develop healthcare technologies. This Dutch- and English-taught pathway emphasises technical models, biomedical measurements, imaging, materials and engineering projects, alongside biological foundations and a final bachelor project.

The first UCR programme combines biomedical science and laboratory work with mathematical modelling, image and data analysis, and general product-design methods. The second places more weight on physiology, disease mechanisms and health evidence. These are related academic routes; they do not supply the specialist mechanics, instrumentation, biomaterials, tissue engineering and integrated healthcare-device projects of TU/e’s technical pathway.

The 45 EC of electives remain open, subject to approval, prior knowledge, non-overlap and level requirements. Entry to the 15-EC final project requires at least 120 EC including compulsory first-year study, completed first- and second-year professional skills, eight later core courses including two second-year CBL projects, and four later elective courses. Results from the immediately preceding exam period do not count for entry.
One required 10-EC skills component spanning two quarter positions, counted once.

Compulsory 15-EC final project in a block in the fourth quarter of year three. Entry includes credit, core-course, elective and professional-skills requirements; immediately preceding exam-period results are excluded.
